messages:
mira chen: hitting a weird one with the python sdk async function invoke — when I call an async function that should return structured output it comes back as a raw string. repro below, using 0.12.3.

mira chen: ```py
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
res = await client.functions.call_async('invoice-extract', {'text': doc})
# expected: parsed dataclass or dict
print(type(res.output))
print(res.output)
```

alex park: can you paste the exact printed output and the headers (if available)? also which python version?

mira chen: python 3.11, prints show <class 'str'> and the string looks like json:

mira chen: ```
'{"amount": 123.45, "currency": "USD", "items": [{"desc": "monthly subscription", "qty": 1}]}'
```

samir bhatt: hmm this smells like a parity/async branch gap — sync call does auto-parse to dict/dataclass when schema is provided, but async path currently returns the raw body for some responses. quick workaround: json.loads(res.output) or client.functions.parse_output(res.output, MySchema) if you have helper.

mira chen: yeah workaround works, but it's confusing for users and breaks typing (annotations expect dict/Invoice). onboarding hit: sample app in the docs shows sync examples only.

jordan li: thanks for the report — I can reproduce locally. opened a fix PR to normalize return type in async calls when content-type is application/json or when a schema/typed-return is provided: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/345 (draft)

jordan li: plan: add unit tests for async path, add an integration test that calls the sample function and asserts we return a dict/dataclass, cut patch v0.12.4 if tests green.

ci-bot: PR #345 — unit tests: passed ✅, integration: flaky on macos runner, re-triggering

mira chen: two small requests: 1) can we add a short sample snippet for async function + dataclass in the python samples repo so customers get a straight example, 2) mention this parity nuance in the migration notes? onboarding pain is real.

alex park: I can add the sample app — will include dataclass example + tiny test. assigning to myself. :thumbsup:

jordan li: perfect. also leaving a note in release notes and the migration guide. we'll aim to have the docs snippet say something like:

jordan li: ```py
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass
class Invoice:
    amount: float
    currency: str
    items: list

res = await client.functions.call_async('invoice-extract', {'text': doc})
# if res.output is str: invoice = Invoice(**json.loads(res.output))
# after fix: res.output will be parsed to dict/dataclass when schema provided
```

mira chen: thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. will validate once the patch lands and update the sample app with a small e2e.

alex park: dropping a small follow-up issue to track adding an explicit type annotation to FunctionResult for async path so mypy/pyright play nice. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789

samir bhatt: note for implementers: watch out for streamed responses — we should only auto-parse for non-streaming responses or provide an opt-in flag to parse. bringing up in the PR review. :eyes:

jordan li: good call. will include a flag and keep current behaviour behind a feature toggle for safety.

mira chen: awesome. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
